ANDHUB ENGINEERING PLC — AI BRAND CONTEXT

Ideas. Engineered.
We turn ideas into solutions that make a difference.

AndHub is a software development, systems engineering, and consultancy company helping businesses of all sizes design, build, and improve the technology and systems they depend on.

From websites and custom software to large-scale business systems, digital products, and expert consultancy, we bring together experienced software developers and systems engineers to solve challenges, simplify operations, and create lasting value.

Backed by experienced leadership in software and systems engineering, we are more than a technology provider. We aim to be a trusted partner that understands your vision, helps shape your ideas, and brings your plans to life.

Different Challenges. Infinite Possibilities. One Hub.

IDENTITY AND WRITING
Formal name: AndHub Engineering PLC; short name: AndHub.
Use AndHub Engineering PLC in formal documents and first mentions; use AndHub thereafter. ANDHUB is the artwork treatment.
Tagline: Ideas. Engineered. Preserve both full stops.
Voice: precise, composed, practical, approachable.
Lead with the problem or outcome, explain the approach, and use specific evidence for capability claims.
Do not invent customers, certifications, partnerships, rankings, performance promises or contact details.

TYPOGRAPHY
Proposed supporting headings: Inter Display. Body/interfaces: Inter. Fallback: Arial, sans-serif.
Inter variable font files are provided in assets/fonts/ with their SIL Open Font License. The historical logo spec records that fonts were not distributed in the original reconstructed pack.
The custom ANDHUB lettering is outlined artwork, not a live-text font. Inter is supporting typography, not an identification of the original wordmark font.

LOGO SYSTEM
Status: Reconstructed artwork for review and approval. Version: 1.0-reconstructed.
Source: User-supplied raster brand identity board.
Layouts:
- symbol: Symbol only; 512 × 512 SVG artboard.
- horizontal: Horizontal / full company name; 1096 × 338 SVG artboard.
- horizontal-tagline: Horizontal / name + tagline; 1096 × 338 SVG artboard.
- stacked: Stacked / full company name; 800 × 613 SVG artboard.
- stacked-tagline: Stacked / name + tagline; 800 × 704 SVG artboard.
- wordmark: Wordmark / full company name, no symbol; 800 × 240 SVG artboard.
- wordmark-tagline: Wordmark / name + tagline, no symbol; 800 × 328 SVG artboard.
- compact: Compact / symbol + ANDHUB, no descriptor; 825 × 240 SVG artboard.
Treatments:
- gradient-light: Gradient / light surfaces; light surface.
- gradient-dark: Gradient / dark surfaces; dark surface.
- flat-light: Flat color / light surfaces; light surface.
- flat-dark: Flat color / dark surfaces; dark surface.
- mono-navy: One color / navy; light surface.
- mono-black: One color / black; light surface.
- mono-white: One color / white reverse; dark surface.
- Resources marked legacy are old logos, raster mockups or historical boards. Use current masters and company data for new work; use legacy resources when historical material is requested.
- Use the supplied logo artwork. Keep its proportions, color order and internal negative spaces intact.
- Choose light/dark artwork for the actual surrounding surface; use a mono treatment for true one-color output.
- Clear space of one quarter of the visible symbol height is a proposed starting standard; verify the chosen reconstructed master.
- Choose compact or symbol-only artwork when the descriptor or tagline becomes unreadable.
- Raster size labels denote the longest artboard edge, including built-in margins.
- Artwork is RGB. Agree print conversions, materials and proofs with the production supplier.
Gradients: Visually approximated from source presentation; not recovered original specifications.

ACCESSIBILITY
Test normal text at 4.5:1 minimum and large text at 3:1 minimum in context.
- #FFFFFF on #2563EB: 5.17:1. Normal text.
- #0B1F3B on #10B981: 6.5:1. Normal text.
- #FFFFFF on #10B981: 2.54:1. Do not use for normal text.
Keep keyboard focus visible, label controls and communicate status beyond color. Test actual components and printed QR codes in their final context.
These recommendations and solid-color ratios do not certify a complete design as accessible.
